```
set -o pipefail\n exec /vc-scheduler ...

set -o pipefail\n sleep inf\n exec /vc-scheduler ...
```

Actually, the `kubectl get pod` shows the args from the Pod spec — this is the CURRENT desired state in the pod template. If someone applied a change to add `sleep inf`, it would update the deployment's pod template but the existing pod would still be running. If a new pod were created, it would have `sleep inf`.

But the pod's `restartCount` is 0 and it was started on May 11. The `sleep inf` must have been added AFTER May 11 to the deployment template but the pod was never recreated.

So the real picture is: the scheduler crashed on May 13, the pod container's main process (the exec'd vc-scheduler) exited, and the pod shows as "Running" because... wait, `exec` replaces PID 1. If `/vc-scheduler` was PID 1 and it exited with Fatal, the container should exit and restart.

Unless the pipe to `/logrotate` kept the container alive. When you do `exec A | B`, the `exec` only replaces the shell for `A`, but the pipe creates subshells.
